1.contenido: Canon 1 We firmly believe and simply confess that there is one true God, eternal and immense, omnipotent, immutable, incomprehensible and ineffable, Father and Son and Holy Spirit: three persons in truth, but one entirely simple essence, substance or nature. The Father of no one, the Son only of the Father, the Holy Spirit equally of both, always without beginning and without end. A single universal Church of the faithful, outside of which no one at all is saved. In which Jesus Christ himself is priest and sacrifice, whose body and blood are truly contained in the sacrament of the altar under the species of bread and wine, the bread being transubstantiated into the body and the wine into the blood by divine power.

2.contenido: Canon 2 We therefore condemn and reprove every heresy that rises up against this holy, orthodox and catholic faith that we have explained above. Condemning all heretics, whatever names they are called.

3.contenido: Canon 3 We excommunicate and anathematize every heresy that rises against this holy, orthodox, Catholic faith. Condemning all heretics, whatever names they are called. Those who are found notably suspicious, unless according to the consideration of the suspicion and the quality of the person they show their own innocence with consistent purgation, are wounded with the sword of anathema and to the point of condign satisfaction are separated from everyone.

4.contenido: Canon 4 We do not condemn the diversity of rites in a single Catholic faith, as long as it is not separated from the unity of faith. We welcome the Greeks and other Easterners into unity, saving their rites that are not contrary to the faith.

5.contenido: Canon 5 Renewing the ancient patriarchal privileges, we sanction that after the Roman Church, which by order of the Lord obtains the principality of ordinary power over all the others, as mother of all the faithful of Christ and teacher, the Constantinopolitan Church obtains the first place, the Alexandrian the second, the Antiochene the third, the Jerusalemite the fourth.

6.contenido: Canon 6 As formerly known to have been instituted by the holy Fathers, the metropolitans must celebrate each year with their suffragan provincial councils. In which they diligently try to correct excesses and reform customs, and also to maintain peace and quiet.

7.contenido: Canon 7 Let the prelates correct the excesses of their subjects, and do not dissemble, lest at the final judgment they be asked to account for their blood. Those who conceal serious crimes are subject to suspension.

8.contenido: Canon 8 In what way and when the prelate should proceed to investigate and punish the excesses of his subjects. Not out of hatred, but out of zeal for justice and charity.

9.contenido: Canon 9 Since in many parts within the same city and diocese there are mixed peoples of different languages, who have various rites and customs under a single faith: we strictly command that the pontiffs of such cities or dioceses provide suitable men who, according to the diversities of rites and languages, celebrate the divine offices for them and minister to them the ecclesiastical sacraments.

10.contenido: Canon 10 Among the other things that concern the salvation of the Christian people, we know that the nourishment of the word of God is very necessary. Therefore we command that the bishops assume suitable men to healthily carry out the office of holy preaching.

11.contenido: Canon 11 Because some, due to poverty, are deprived of the study of reading and the opportunity to progress, in each cathedral church and in others whose sufficiency allows it, a teacher be provided to teach free of charge to clerics and poor schoolchildren.

21.contenido: Canon 21 of confessione Every faithful of either sex, after he has reached the years of discretion, faithfully confesses all his sins alone, at least once a year, to his own priest, and strives to fulfill according to his strength the penance imposed on him, reverently receiving at least at Easter the sacrament of the Eucharist, unless by the advice of the priest himself, for some reasonable cause, he has decided to abstain for a time from its reception; Otherwise, in life he will be excluded from entering the church and when he dies he will lack a Christian burial. Therefore, let this salutary statute be frequently published in the churches, so that no one assumes the veil of excuse through the blindness of ignorance.

62.contenido: Canon 62 of reliquiis Since by the fact that some expose relics of saints for sale and show them everywhere, the Christian religion has often been detracted: so that it is not detracted from now on, by this decree we establish that ancient relics from now on will not be displayed outside the reliquary or exposed for sale. No one dares to publish those found again, unless they have first been approved by the authority of the Roman Pontiff.

68.contenido: Canon 68 of Iudaeis In some provinces the diversity of habit has distinguished the Jews from the Christians, but in others a certain confusion has taken root so that they are not distinguished by any difference. Hence it sometimes happens that by mistake Christians mix with the wives of Jews, and Jews with the wives of Christians. So that the excesses of such a condemnable mixture may no longer find refuge as an excuse under the veil of such an error, we establish that such persons of both sexes, in every province of Christians and at all times, be publicly distinguished from other peoples by the quality of their habit.
